reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports a non-monotonic relationship and the benefit of moderate negative misfit in HESAs, but it does not address multilayer coatings, the specific misfit values proposed (-0.14%, -0.30%, +0.14%), or the 200 nm thickness boundary; the hypothesis overstates the direct applicability of the evidence to its specific system and conditions.
premises: A moderate negative lattice misfit (-0.14%) enhances interface coherency and dislocation pinning in HEA multilayers
An excessively negative misfit (-0.30%) or a positive misfit (+0.14%) leads to incoherent interfaces and increased dislocation transmission
The relationship between misfit magnitude and creep resistance is non-monotonic, with an optimum at moderate negative misfit
Negative misfit is generally more effective than positive misfit in resisting creep by strengthening interfaces
These misfit effects apply to multilayer coatings with layer thickness below 200 nm at 700°C
